entries.title: Proverbs 10:1
segments:
The Proverbs of Solomon; here begins the second division of this book, extending the sixteenth verse of the twenty-second chapter. 
 
  A wise son; in this proverb, as in many of the following, the two clauses must be mutually supplied, each from the other, thus: A wise son maketh glad both father and mother; but a foolish son is the heaviness of both. 
 
Since the happiness or misery of parents depends so much upon the character and conduct of their children, this should be an incitement to them diligently to train them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:2
segments:
Treasures of wickedness; wealth wrongfully gotten. 
 
  Delivereth from death; from violent and premature death, which is often threatened as the punishment of the wicked,

.  The words also include the promise of deliverance from eternal death, of which all less deliverances are but pledges and earnests. 
 
The curse of God rests upon all unrighteous gain.  It can confer upon its owners no true happiness in this world, and it exposes them to his everlasting displeasure in the world to come.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:4
segments: The general law of God's moral government is, industry and plenty, poverty and want.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:5
segments: A principal part of wisdom lies in discerning and improving passing opportunities.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:6
segments: Covereth the mouth of the wicked; that is, his mouth is filled with violence, by which he brings upon himself the curses of his fellow-men.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:7
segments: A permanent good mane can be gained only by righteousness.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:8
segments:
Will receive commandments--shall fall; here, as often in these proverbs, the first clause gives the character of a wise man; the second, the end of a fool.  Fill out the two clauses thus: The wise in heart will receive commandments, therefore he shall stand firm; but a prating fool will not hear advice, therefore he shall fall. 
 
He who is more ready to talk than to take advice is near destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:9
segments:
Shall be known; exposed and punished. 
 
All crooked practices will in the end be detected and punished.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:10
segments: Winketh with the eye; a sign of malicious cunning.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:12
segments: Love is the great principle of harmony; it disposes men to cover the faults of their neighbors, and deal leniently with them.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:13
segments: He who will not be corrected by God's word must feel his rod.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:14
segments:
Lay up knowledge; which keeps them from speaking unadvisedly. 
 
  Near destruction; constantly exposes them to destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:15
segments: Destruction of the poor; that which exposes them to much injury from wicked men.  This is not inconsistent with the promise, that God will protect the pious poor who put their trust in him.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:17
segments: The unteachable are in the road to certain ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:19
segments: Wisdom is shown not less in what we forbear to utter, than in what we say.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:20
segments:
As choice silver; from the rich treasury of his heart he brings forth words that are as choice silver. 
 
  Heart--is little worth; and therefore his words also are destitute of worth.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:22
segments: True prosperity flows from God's presence and blessing.  Without this all apparent success will but multiply our troubles.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:23
segments: Hath wisdom; which leads him to abhor mischief.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:24
segments: Under the righteous government of God, the highest hopes of the righteous and the worst fears of the wicked shall be more than realized.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:25
segments: Is an everlasting foundation; his blessedness rests on the immovable foundation of God's promises.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:29
segments: The way of the Lord; either God's way of acting, or the way which he prescribes to men.  In the former sense the meaning will be, that God's providence protects the upright; in the latter, that obedience to God secures his protection.

entries.title: Proverbs 10:30
segments: Inhabit the earth; in its original meaning, dwell securely in the promised land.
But the words contain a general promise of peace and prosperity to the righteous.  See note to

entries.title: Proverbs 10:31
segments: Bringeth forth wisdom--shall be cut out; fill out the two clauses thus: bringeth forth wisdom, and therefore is acceptable to God and man; speaketh folly, and therefore shall be cut out.  See note to
